title: Naming the open strings
summary: The six open strings are E, A, D, G, B and E, from thickest to thinnest.

steps.title: What tuning means
steps.body:
**Tuning** is the set of notes your open strings are set to. Turning a tuning peg tightens or loosens a string, which raises or lowers its note.

**Why it matters:** Chords and scales only sound right when the strings are in tune. If your band says "tune up", they mean get every open string to its right note.

steps.title: Standard tuning
steps.body:
Most guitars use **standard tuning**. From the thickest string to the thinnest, the open strings are E, A, D, G, B and E. A handy way to remember them: Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie.

**Why it matters:** Nearly all songs and lessons assume standard tuning, so these six names are what you will use every day.

steps.title: Both E strings
steps.body: The thickest and the thinnest strings are both E. They sound the same letter, two octaves apart.

items.prompt: Play the lit note. It is the open A string.
Play the lit note. It is the open G string.
Play the lit note. It is the open B string.

steps.title: Say it as you play
steps.body: Pluck each open string and say its name out loud: E, A, D, G, B, E.
